messages.author: 1cd3ce37d8489fec
messages.subject: Pystan parallelization status
parts:
Hello,

I have a question about the status of parallelization in Pystan v.2.0.1.2.  The n_jobs parameter of pystan.stan says, in the docstring, "Sample in parallel."  My expectation is that this means multiple cores will be used to sample from multiple chains in parallel, and the other (more complicated) possibility would seem to be that it parallelizes some of the sampling steps within individual chains. But in my tests it's not clear to me that either is working.

What I find is that, regardless of the value of n_jobs, only 1 core on my CPU seems to be utilized and the chains seem to sample in serial.  Additionally, the sampling time reported by Pystan seems to be the same either way, so I don't think there is any speedup.  I do see that model.py imports and uses multiprocessing, and I can confirm that this python module is installed on my system.

Below I have pasted example input and output using the 8 schools model and data from the Pystan Getting Started page.

A related problem is that when I specify chains > 1, I seem to get a TypeError after the sampling succesfully finishes (see below).

Thanks in advance for any information!

Best,

~Nathan

messages.author: 1cd3ce37d8489fec
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pystan parallelization status
parts:
Hi Allen,

Thanks for diagnosing this bug, and suggesting the sampling method, which seems to be working!

As a follow up, I'm still not clear on how the parallelization is achieved.  Using the sampling workaround, Pystan still prints out the status and completion times of each chain in sequence, leading me to believe that the sampling within each chain is being parallelized.  However, I have found that (regardless of the value of n_jobs used), Pystan seems to be leveraging a number of cores on my machine equal to the number of chains I specify (i.e. 1 core if I set chains=1, 3 if I set chains=3, etc.).  That would seem to instead suggest that chains are being run in parallel.

If I am correct that sampling within chains is parallelized, am I encountering a bug or mis-understanding how the parameters are specified?  Or are the chains run in parallel and I am mis-understanding the Pystan command line output?
Thanks in advance for any information!

P.S. for posterity, the TypeError was due to passing a float for the number of samples to the Pystan sampling method.  Allen has now merged a fix for this (https://github.com/stan-dev/pystan/commit/d003682c8df4f4896c124201d940a92b9f508a09)

On Thursday, December 12, 2013 9:34:11 PM UTC-5, Allen Riddell wrote:
Hi Nathan,

I found the bug. I'll push out a fix shortly. If you want to do parallel
sampling right now just compile the model (StanModel) and then use the sampling
method with n_jobs.

As for the TypeError. There are a few NumPy tickets that refer to it. Thanks for
pointing it out.

Best,

-a

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pystan parallelization status
parts:
Hi Allen,

Thanks for this fix! I've been testing fits with the new release this
morning, and (to answer my earlier question) the revised logging makes
it clear that parallelization is achieved by launching multiple chains
in parallel.

It's a little confusing that sampling status is reported for one chain
at a time, which makes it seem as though the chains are being run in
sequence (because the logging switches to the next active chain after
the first one finishes). In case anyone else shares my confusion,
I've tried to make this more clear by updating the doc string and
adding a warning - see this pull request:

https://github.com/stan-dev/pystan/pull/49

On Wed, Dec 18, 2013 at 6:27 PM, Allen Riddell <a...@ariddell.org> wrote:
> Currently the only way to tell that sampling is occurring in parallel is to
> notice that all your cores are in use. There should be a message to avoid any
> confusion. I'll add one right now.
>
> Thanks,
>
> -a
>

>> Using the sampling workaround, Pystan still prints out the status and

>> sampling within each chain is being parallelized. However, I have found

>> leveraging a number of cores on my machine equal to the number of chains I
>> specify (i.e. 1 core if I set chains=1, 3 if I set chains=3, etc.). That
>> would seem to instead suggest that chains are being run in parallel.
>>

>> encountering a bug or mis-understanding how the parameters are specified?
>> Or are the chains run in parallel and I am mis-understanding the Pystan
>> command line output?
